title: id Software dev says mass layoffs like Microsoft's are weakening the games industry, because developers 'don't have the incentive to care anymore'
summary: "A lot of gamers, even if they don't know it, they can feel it's not right. There's something wrong."
body: At the end of last month, id Software lead services programmer Chris Hayes offered a blunt appraisal of Xbox's management during an interview with YouTube channel Auf ein Bier, saying Microsoft's repeated mass layoffs have proved that its leadership "fundamentally don't understand art." Elsewhere in the interview, Hayes expanded the scope of his criticism beyond the immediate damage wrought by the latest round of Xbox cuts . Looking at the industry more broadly, Hayes, who's still a Microsoft employee, says mass layoffs and nearsighted cost cutting are producing worse games, because they're denying game developers the opportunity—and motivation—to improve their craft. While major companies like Microsoft might brag about the "great IPs and studios" that they own, Hayes said they seem incapable of understanding that they regularly harm their own capability to produce anything of value with those brands and developers. "It is our experience together, our working together, and our past experiences that make the studio good. Yeah, you could just throw away half [of your developers] and bring in more later if you happen to need more number of hours to fill out the check boxes that you …

title: 'Thank you so much for the best weekend ever': The id Software gang got together at QuakeCon, and it sure looks like everyone had a great time
summary: I love a happy ending.
body: The recently concluded QuakeCon was a big one, marking the 30th anniversary of the game that started it all and, more notably, bringing id Software co-founders Adrian Carmack, John Carmack, Tom Hall, and John Romero together for the first time in a very long time. I had wondered, in the lead-up to the event, if it might get a little awkward or uncomfortable: Differences between the Johns were " over-dramatized " over the years, according to Romero Games co-founder Brenda Romero, but Adrian Carmack filed a lawsuit over his removal from the studio back in 2005, and other internal conflicts over the years led to the dismissal of well-liked employees like American McGee and Paul Steed. The more recent layoffs of Xbox that left the studio in varying states of " gutted ," depending on who you ask, also threatened to overshadow the whole thing. So, you know: you wonder . Now that everything is wrapped up, I'm happy to report that if there was any awkwardness or discomfort between the studio's famed founders, everyone kept it to themselves and they all seemed to have a really good time. "QuakeCon was fantastic this year, especially reuniting with the original founders!" John Carmack wrote…

body: The new Arc Raiders Phantom Targets project is all about helping Shani track and trace some mysterious arc that seem to be popping up across topside. title: Corsair isn't rolling in money from its mega-expensive RAM kits—and it's all thanks to higher component costs and lower demand
summary: The memory crisis is a complicated beast.
body: If you've looked at memory prices recently, you've probably seen Corsair DIMMs selling for astonishing prices. The 32 GB Vengeance DDR5 RGB kit sitting in my PC right now is selling for $480 at Amazon , whereas I bought it for $90-$100 just a couple of years ago. Corsair RAM can still be some of the cheapest comparatively , but it's very pricey nonetheless. So, Corsair must be raking in money hand over fist, right? Not quite, at least according to its recent filings with the SEC . The figures show a ~9% decline in Q2 2026 gaming component and system revenue overall compared to last year—although gross profit was up 17%. Memory revenue itself has increased, but its "other component products" revenue has decreased significantly. According to the company: "We are both a seller of memory products and a purchaser of memory and other components from third-party suppliers. As a result, elevated pricing benefits net sales and margin on the memory products we sell, while also increasing our cost of components across our broader product offerings." title: Dev at id Software says Microsoft 'burned a lot of bridges' in the industry: 'They fundamentally don't understand art, they don't understand games'
summary: "The way they align their spreadsheets for their financial reports—is not the way we used to do it."
body: One of the biggest tragedies of Xbox's wide-reaching reset is id Software, which was cut by a whopping 136 roles . And while official statements from Microsoft and the studio have tried to reassure players that it's not been gutted , whether that's just a panicking Xbox trying to calm anxieties is up for debate. Especially given the words of Chris Hays, lead services programmer at id Software, in an interview with YouTube channel Auf ein Bier at the end of last month. To say that Hays doesn't mince his words is an understatement—and I'm finding it hard to blame him, given Microsoft announced the layoffs one day before Doom: The Dark Ages released its DLC . " Everyone had just gotten off of a worse-than-usual crunch to get the DLC out the door, finally get a breather, and we were excited for our launch on the Tuesday … Instead of watching in anticipation for people, streamers, and seeing all the hard work they put in finally pay off? Now they don't know what they're doing." title: Valve has added 'initial' SteamOS gamepad support for several new gaming handhelds, including the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+
summary: Along with a host of bug fixes, of course.
body: Valve is still beavering away at the internals of SteamOS, and the latest update notes for the 3.8.25 Beta release mention the addition of "initial gamepad support" for several non-Valve gaming handhelds. The mighty MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ is on the list, as are two offerings from Ayaneo. These are the Ayaneo Pocket S2 , an Android-first, Snapdragon-powered device that launched in June of last year, and the Konkr Fit , a recently-launched Windows handheld released under one of Ayaeno's sub-brands. The Fit comes in two AMD APU flavours, the Ryzen AI 9 HX 470 and the Ryzen AI 9 HX 370. It's also got TMR joysticks and Hall effect triggers, which should hopefully benefit from the latest update. Tucked away at the bottom of the "Non-Valve Devices" section is a note on updated gamepad support for the OneXPlayer Apex . You know, the one with an optional plug-in liquid cooling tower released back in the pre-memory crisis times, when ultra-high-end handhelds made a small modicum of sense. Anyway, it seems Valve is working hard on SteamOS compatibility with the latest handheld releases —even if they're increasingly looking like some of the biggest victims of the RAMpocalypse so far. title: Blizzard is now reportedly Microsoft's top studio, according to leaked email
summary: "This past year has marked our third highest fiscal for top line revenue in Blizzard's history."
body: The studio behind Warcraft, Diablo, and Overwatch just had its third-biggest year for top line revenue ever, according to a leaked email. The email (via Windows Central ) reportedly contained Blizzard president Johanna Faries praising the team for finishing off FY26 as "the top-performing studio in Xbox's studios division." "Diablo 4: Lord of Hatred and Overwatch drove exceptional performance in particular, with Overwatch delivering its strongest quarter since 2022," she wrote. She said Overwatch has been growing for multiple consecutive years for the first time since its release, and that Blizzcon 2026 should "serve as a powerful springboard into a new era of momentum." Notably, this success is despite the fact that Microsoft is a pressure target and Xbox is a priority target of the BDS movement protesting the involvement of corporations in Israel's ongoing genocide of Palestinians. And while Blizzard seemingly hasn't been pummeled by Xbox's 3,200-layoff "reset" the way studios like Double Fine and Zenimax have, a huge portion of the job cuts have yet to land . body: Disk Cleanup (Image credit: Future) Welcome to Disk Cleanup , our regular weekend feature delving into the PCs of PC gaming luminaries. Come back every weekend to read a new interview, digging into the important questions, like "How tidy is your desktop?" and "What game will you never uninstall?" Sam Barlow is the director of Half Mermaid and one of interactive fiction's modern luminaries. Breaking into game development with his one-move choose your own adventure Arrival, Barlow worked on games like Ghost Rider and Silent Hill: Shattered Memories before striking out on his own with 2015's Her Story . Blending FMV-style video with an investigative branching narrative, Her Story was a pioneer in the detective game genre. Since Her Story, Barlow has further experimented with combining live-action footage and interactive fiction in 2019's Telling Lies and 2021's Immortality. title: Cancelled Quake 4 expansion gets surprise GitHub release after former XCOM 2 developer discovers it on an old hard drive: 'This essentially saved my life'
summary: Quake 4: Awakening was in development at Ritual Entertainment before being scrapped.
body: Typical, isn't it? You wait ages for a surprise launch of additional Quake adventures, and then two come along at once. The original game just received an official new episode as part of the shooter's 30 th anniversary celebrations taking place at this year's QuakeCon. But now Raven Software's Quake 4 has got in on the action, as a build of the sequel's cancelled expansion has been discovered and uploaded to GitHub . Quake 4: Awakening was being developed at Ritual Entertainment—creators of the soon to be remastered SiN and its aborted episodic sequel—but the project was canned by Activision due to underwhelming sales of the base game. The expansion was thought lost to time, until a veteran game developer chanced upon a copy on the hard drive of a second-hand PC he bought. Said developer is Justin Marshall, a programmer who has worked on games such as The Evil Within , XCOM 2 , Dead Island 2 , and The Dark Pictures Anthology —and unfortunately is one of the casualties of the industry's massive swathe of layoffs. title: Roblox shares plummet by 70% after the company reports persistent decline in player numbers, and of course the solution involves AI
summary: The company's earnings outlook for the remaining year has "changed considerably."
body: The seemingly unstoppable force that is Roblox might not be so unstoppable after all. The company share price has dropped by 70% following the publication of its second-quarter earnings, which show a decline in players and lower-than-expected monetisation. In an earnings call (via Games Industry ) Roblox CFO Naveen Chopra said the company attributed the shortfall to a dearth of "vintage viral games", with players shifting attention to "new and evergreen experiences with lower hourly monetisation". This was exacerbated by changes in Roblox's recommendation algorithm, which Chopra says "optimises for long-term retention" at the expense of "near-term monetisation". While Roblox still has an enormous audience of 123 million daily players, this number has declined steadily across the previous three quarters from a high of 152 million. Monthly unique players have also fallen by 10 million in the last two quarters, with the number currently at 27 million. Roblox doesn't expect these winds to change in the near future, either. The company forecasts a year-on-year decline of between 14% and 18% in its third quarter, with Chopra saying that "monetisation weakness is likely to continue." It …

title: The GTA 3D trilogy fanpatch has its biggest update, with over 100 new fixes including restored dialogue for San Andreas
summary: Here we go again.
body: It's well-known that the PC ports of GTA 3, Vice City, and San Andreas were a shemozzle, thanks in part to re-used code across the trio of games, but also a general lack of care that used to be the norm when it came to PC ports. The excellent SilentPatch has long been the solution, and it's now even better thanks to a significant update that not only fixes leftover bugs, but also restores cut content that was inaccessible thanks to typos in the code. One big change you'll notice with this version of the patch is that 100 voice lines have been restored to GTA San Andreas. Some of these were only bugged in a specific circumstance—like the lines CJ says when shooting at people, which only worked if you played with a controller. Those lines will now trigger when you pull the trigger when aiming with mouse and keyboard. A lot of other dialogue that would otherwise never be heard has been restored too. body: Weird Weekend Weird Weekend is our regular Saturday column where we celebrate PC gaming oddities: peculiar games, strange bits of trivia, forgotten history. Pop back every weekend to find out what Jeremy, Josh, Ted, and Rick have become obsessed with this time, whether it's the canon height of Thief's Garrett or that time someone in the Vatican pirated Football Manager . A Game of Thrones CRPG is such an obvious licensing fit and yet, culturally and corporately, always appears to be two zigs and a zag away from actually happening. Perhaps Warhorse Studios was the most likely candidate, in the wake of two unflinching medieval simulations under the Kingdom Come banner. But the Czech studio's owner, Embracer, is also cradling the clumsily named Middle-earth Enterprises, and so Warhorse's future belongs to The Lord of the Rings. title: Blocky zombie survival sim Unturned releases its source code so players can build a 'lasting legacy' for the game 'regardless of the changes we make'
summary: The source files are freely available for non-commercial use.
body: Smartly Dressed Games, developer of the wildly popular free-to-play zombie survival sim Unturned, has released the game's source code for non-commercial use. "Unturned's source code and project files are now freely available!" the developers wrote in a Steam post . "Whether you have a new feature or total conversion in mind, the sky's the limit." The source code is available via GitHub . In an accompanying FAQ , Smartly Dressed Games explained that the reason behind the release is to further support the community's creative efforts. "Unturned's greatest strength is our passionate community," the studio wrote. "Releasing the source files allows you and other players to further expand upon the game as you see fit, building a lasting legacy for the game regardless of the changes we make or how many years pass." There are some conditions for players and modders who want to use the source code. In the FAQ, Smartly Dressed Games stressed that uses for the source code "must be strictly non-commercial" and that "players must be able to play and access all features and content of your mod for free."
